headline: HMC Capital CEO Sid Sharma bullish on HomeCo REIT outlook despite FY27 FFO dip driven by interest rate headwinds
reasoning: Sharma describes FY26 as a year of disciplined operational excellence, with FFO of $0.09 per unit and distributions of 8.6 cents, both in line with guidance. He acknowledges a moderate 2% dip in FFO to 8.8 cents in FY27 driven by higher financing costs, noting the trust has absorbed the interest rate headwind upfront. Despite this, he is bullish on the operational outlook, citing strong tenant sales, rising foot traffic, and no observable correlation between consumer sentiment and consumer spending. He notes July and August trading has been remarkably stronger than Q3 and Q4 of FY26, and expects retailers to outperform consensus expectations over the next six months. Rental growth is expected to remain predictable and growing, underpinned by structural undersupply of high-quality retail space and occupancy running well in excess of 99% across the sector. The trust may selectively divest one or two assets trading inside cost of debt, which could be earnings accretive.
quote: No. 2026 was just another year of disciplined operational excellence. Our centers are performing well. More importantly, our retailers are performing well. So we've delivered on our guidance for FY 26 of $0.09 per unit. I suppose with with everyone else in the real estate sector, what's in front of us? There's some interest expense headwinds in FY 27. So our guidance next year or sorry, this year compared to 26 shows a moderate, uh, moderate pullback on the FFO per unit from $0.09 to 8.8 cents. Um, but really, what's happening in the assets is still quite remarkable. Um, the consumers are spending and there's no correlation really, that we can see between consumer sentiment and consumer spending. So tenant sales are up. Expenditures are foot traffic's up. Um, so we're actually, you know, pretty bullish about the outlook this year.
episode_title: HomeCo. REIT keeps its footing as rates bite

headline: HMC Capital absorbing interest expense headwinds now to rebase earnings and grow from FY28, with selective asset divestments likely to be accretive
reasoning: Sid Sharma explained that while HMC's debt levels are relatively low at this point in the cycle, the group has decided to absorb interest expense headwinds earlier than most peers, effectively rebasing earnings now. He noted that selective divestment of one or two assets trading inside the cost of debt is likely to be earnings accretive and could support earnings growth over the coming year. Looking out to FY28 and FY29, Sharma expressed confidence that earnings would rebound quickly. He also highlighted that portfolio valuations continue to increase given the rarity and strong demand for the group's large format retail assets, which serve growth suburbs in Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane.
quote: Interest expense headwinds are going to be an issue for a lot of groups moving forward. And we're one of the groups that are reported a bit earlier. And, you know, some some groups might absorb some of that in future years. Some will absorb it. Now, we've decided to, to to absorb that interest expense headwind earlier than most. And, and you know, effectively to rebase and then grow from here. So if I look at 28, if I look at 29, um, with everything I know in front of me, our earnings and will rebound pretty quickly. Um, but nonetheless, you know, our valuations are still going to go up. These assets are very much in demand and are very rare. Very, very rare to find.
episode_title: HomeCo. REIT keeps its footing as rates bite

headline: Sid Sharma flags upside risks to interest rates remain, with consensus having shifted away from the expected downward trend
reasoning: Sharma notes that 12 months ago the market consensus assumed interest rates were on a downward trend heading into calendar year 2026, but the world has changed. He defers to those with more experience on the interest rate outlook but observes that consensus now sees risks as skewed to the upside on rates, not the downside. This rate environment has been the primary driver of the FFO headwind absorbed into FY27 guidance.
quote: If we go back 12 months, everyone assumed that we were on the downward trend on interest rates heading into, you know, calendar year 26. Obviously, the world's a unique place at the moment. And, you know, folks that are are much more experience than me can comment upon the interest rate outlook. Um, but if you listen to the consensus, the risks are to the upside on interest rates, not the downside. Um, so what we've done is we've really absorbed that interest rate headwind that would have been coming later anyway. We've absorbed it straight away. And that's what really drives the dip in FFO from 9 to 8.8 cents for the coming year.
episode_title: HomeCo. REIT keeps its footing as rates bite

headline: Sid Sharma highlights structural undersupply of high-quality retail space driving persistent occupancy above 99% and strong tenant demand
reasoning: Sharma points out that very little new retail product is being built, creating a complete undersupply of high-quality retail space across Australia. This has pushed occupancy rates well in excess of 99% not just for HomeCo but across all shopping centres. Major anchor tenants including Woolworths, Coles, Anaconda, Baby Bunting, Harvey Norman and Next rely on physical store networks as the most cost-effective way to serve customers, sustaining strong tenant demand. Population growth concentrated in Sydney and Melbourne, where approximately 50% of HomeCo's assets are located, provides an additional structural tailwind for visitation and spend.
quote: Unfortunately for retailers, what's really hard right now is known as building much new product. We're one of the few retail development groups that creates new space, but there's just not a lot of it. So there's a complete undersupply of high quality retail space and occupancy, not just with our portfolio, but with all shopping centres is running well in excess of 99%. So tenant demand, whether it's from the Woolworths or the Coles or whether it's from, you know, the anacondas and the baby buntings or the Harvey Norman's and the next gullies remains really strong because in order for them to serve their customers, the store network is still the most optimal, cost effective way to deliver product to the consumer. So that demand is what's going to keep driving our rental growth and ultimately our developments.
episode_title: HomeCo. REIT keeps its footing as rates bite

headline: Sid Sharma sees strong consumer spending momentum in July-August 2026, with spending patterns normalising despite choppy interest rate environment
reasoning: Sharma observes a disconnect between consumer sentiment and actual consumer spending, with tenant sales and foot traffic both rising. He notes that July and August 2026 trading has been remarkably stronger than Q3 and Q4 of FY26. His interpretation is that consumers have adjusted their wallets and spending patterns in response to the uncertain rate environment and are now beginning to spend again. He expects retailers to outperform consensus expectations over the next six months, which will in turn support predictable and growing rental income for HomeCo.
quote: What's interesting in the medium term is retail spending is still strong. July and August has been remarkably stronger than quarter three and quarter four of FY 26. So what does that mean? I think the consumers understood that we're in a choppy interest rate environment. They're adjusting their wallets and adjusting their behaviors and patterns of spend, and they're starting to spend it again. So I do expect retailers will do better than we all think they will for the next six months.
episode_title: HomeCo. REIT keeps its footing as rates bite
